phase: Reader quality of life and expressive authoring
objective: Search installed fonts; configure auto-advance time; author diegetic dialogue-panel images; style and animate individual words; stage autonomous ambient scenery actors.
status: verified complete: QOL01–QOL08 certified on merged main; final narrative and Bevy CI green

rules.execution: Implementation ongoing under the project stewardship protocol; credit only after acceptance-specific CI and merged-main certification.
rules.architecture: Rust + Bevy 0.20; pure Rust narrative parser; external game-relative .vn/TOML/images/audio/fonts; generic engine; no game-specific Rust branches.
rules.performance: Never block UI/render with font/file discovery, disk I/O, image generation, parsing or unbounded per-frame allocations. Cache or worker-load slow data; cap animated spans, texture resources and ECS entities.
rules.safety: Validate untrusted game paths against root, including traversal/symlinks; reject invalid numeric values and malformed markup with useful diagnostics.
rules.compatibility: Keep three existing examples, old saves, existing preference files, and authored theme fallback working; use optional fields/migration where necessary.
rules.accessibility: Honor high contrast and reduced motion, accessible readable static effects, keyboard-first plus pointer input, proper font fallback.
rules.platform: EndeavourOS/Arch/Hyprland/Linux-first, free/local. No paid API, Mac requirement, npm, mandatory custom shaders, runtime AI or WYSIWYG editor.
rules.verification: Earn weight only on tests plus appropriate visual evidence and a green source commit; final complete requires both jobs green on main, not a plan.

design_notes: QOL01: searchable installed-font picker now merged, with cached discovery, incremental filter, preview and persistence.
QOL02: 0.5–20.0-second configurable auto-advance delay now merged; 1.5 seconds remains the default.
Bevy 0.20 has official system-font discovery and TextSpan; TextSpan supports per-span style but not automatically per-glyph offset animation.
Proposed text syntax is illustrative only until the QOL04 grammar is specified; authored effects must preserve a plain accessible text stream.
Ambient actors are finite author-directed stage motion, not pathfinding or AI.
Kentucky Route Zero, Celeste and Hollow Knight are cited only as inspirations for expressive text, never sources of copied art or code.
non_goals: Skeletal rigs, 3D scenes, pathfinding AI or collision simulation
Unrestricted disk font imports as game assets
Mandatory GPU shaders or paid/cloud dependencies
Unbounded effects/spawns or heavy update-thread work

tasks.title: Searchable installed-font browser
tasks.goal: Replace the hard-coded family cycle with a searchable, previewable browser of truly installed system fonts.
acceptance: Appearance Settings contains a focused search input, case-insensitive incremental filtering, scrollable installed-family list, selected/current indicators, live specimen, and keyboard/mouse activation.

Enumerate Bevy 0.20 system-font families using a cached discovery catalog; sort/deduplicate and never scan font directories or resolve large catalogs every frame. Zero/one/many-font hosts are handled.

Persist chosen installed family through existing validated atomic player preferences; missing/uninstalled fonts fall back to the author's font and generic fallback, including multilingual glyph coverage; no arbitrary filesystem paths.
Bevy input/screenshot QA proves search, preview, selection, restart persistence, missing-font fallback, long/Unicode names and unchanged old-game behavior.
tasks.example: Search 'DejaVu', preview matching fonts immediately, select one, and keep it on restart.

tasks.title: Player-controlled auto-advance wait
tasks.goal: Replace the current hard-coded 1.5-second hold with a persistent reader setting.
acceptance: Appearance offers Auto-advance delay: 0.5–20.0 seconds in 0.5-second increments, with a visible value and Reset; auto-advance remains separately opt-in and the old default stays 1.5s.
Countdown begins only when the final grapheme has appeared; user interaction/scene change restarts it; pause, settings, history, saves and manual interaction suspend/reset it safely.
Choices, unanswered prompts and endings never auto-select; no double advance when user presses Enter during or at timer expiration.
New optional preference validates finite bounded values; legacy preferences and v1 story saves still load; deterministic clock tests plus GUI and cross-restart regressions pass.
tasks.example: With auto advance enabled and delay 4.5s, a line remains fully visible for 4.5s before moving on.

tasks.title: Inline style-span authoring foundation
tasks.goal: Let authors target individual words/phrases without changing or styling an entire line.
acceptance: Specify an optional escaped inline markup grammar in quoted .vn dialogue, with named styles, clear nesting/adjacency rules and file/line diagnostics for bad or unknown tags.

Keep a clear plain-text representation for accessibility/history and structured span data for presentation; preserve Unicode grapheme-safe reveal, wrapping, measured glyph bounds, source fingerprint/hot reload and legacy save compatibility.
Use Bevy TextSpan for supported per-span font/color; explicitly isolate effects needing per-glyph offset because TextSpan does not itself solve animated displacement.
Unit tests cover quoted escapes, malformed/nested markup, ZWJ emoji, combining marks, multilingual dialogue, parser validation and six-size visual layout; unmarked stories render unchanged.

tasks.title: Per-word dynamic flair library
tasks.goal: Provide reusable theme-defined fiery, dark, wavering and shimmering words, inspired conceptually by expressive game typography.
acceptance: Implement static color/emphasis and at least three bounded dynamic effects such as ember flicker, shadow/dim, and gentle wave/tremble, with per-theme validated color, amplitude, rate and timing settings.
Different marked words can coexist on a line without text reflow, glyph splitting, clipping or broken reveal/choices; expensive shaping and parsing are not repeated each frame.
High-contrast mode and reduced motion override authored effects with readable static equivalents; pause, skip, hot reload and settings changes have deterministic behavior.
Set finite active span/glyph caps and measure the worst authored case; visual masks and unit tests cover multibyte glyphs, long wraps, color/contrast, animation frames and no per-frame I/O.
tasks.example: A word glows/flickers like ember; a separate word looks darkened; reduced motion shows both clearly as static text.

tasks.title: Independent ambient-scene actor infrastructure
tasks.goal: Put birds, background NPCs, vehicles and other scenery actors on stage independently of dialogue characters or motes.
acceptance: Author-side manifest declares ambient IDs, sprite assets, scale, anchor, depth/layer, opacity, optional scene association, show/hide and bounded start phase; engine stays game-neutral.
Loading, spawning, scene switching, hiding, restoring, save/reload and hot reload of ambient entities are deterministic and independent of foreground speaking actors.
Validate secure root-contained image paths, finite scale/coordinates, capped active actors (target 24) and missing assets; old games that declare none render unchanged.
Bevy smoke screenshots verify correct layer order, lifecycle, scene switching, responsive cover/crop alignment, pause/reduced-motion behavior and no blocking update-thread I/O.

tasks.title: Autonomous ambient motion and flipbook frames
tasks.goal: Let an NPC patrol, birds fly, and a plane cross the scene on their own with no per-frame story scripting.
acceptance: Provide finite authored waypoint/linear paths, loops/ping-pong/one-shot modes, speed or period, staggered repeat phases, facing/flip and optional bounded sprite-frame animation.
Ship three test motions: walking background NPC, looping bird flight, and one-shot plane traverse; all operate independently of input and coexist with characters and particles.

Time-based updates are framerate-independent and bounded; pause freezes motion; reduced motion freezes a meaningful pose or hides decoration; changes survive resize, save/load and hot reload predictably.

Limit number of actors, path points, frames, speeds and texture usage; exclude pathfinding, collision physics, unlimited spawns or runtime image generation; screenshots capture start/middle/end and pause.
